purpose: Canonical example for epic quality. Use as a guide for evaluating epics (strategic initiatives spanning multiple sprints).

epic.title: Invoice self-service
epic.goal: Enable residential customers to independently access, view, and download their invoices by Q2/2026, reducing support demand for invoice copies by 30%.

benefit.customers: Save 10 minutes per month by self-serving invoices (no more support calls for invoice requests)
benefit.supportTeam: Reduce workload by 50 tickets/month (from 150 to 100 invoice-related tickets)
benefit.business: No additional headcount needed for invoice requests; improved customer satisfaction (NPS +5 points)

childStories.title: Provide an overview of annual expenses

risks.mitigation: Proactive communication campaign, in-app tutorials, support team training

risks.risk: Technical debt in legacy invoice system
risks.mitigation: Early spike on legacy code, buffer time in timeline for refactoring
Early involvement of legal team (Anna), compliance check at MVP milestone

goalStatement.evidence: SMART goal: Specific (enable customers to access invoices), Measurable (30% reduction in support tickets), Time-bound (by Q2/2026).

benefitStatement.evidence: Quantified benefits for 3 stakeholder groups: customers (10 min/month), support team (50 tickets/month), business (NPS +5, no headcount increase).

storyList.evidence: 4 child stories linked (#2, #7, #11, #13) with status tracking (2 Done, 1 In Progress, 1 Backlog).

successMetrics.evidence: 1 primary metric + 3 secondary metrics, all with baseline, target, and deadline.

stakeholders.evidence: Owner (PM), Tech Lead, and 3 key stakeholders named with roles.

timeline.evidence: Clear start/end dates, 3 milestones with story mapping.

acTestability.evidence: Epic success is testable: 30% ticket reduction, 80% adoption, <2% error rate – all measurable.

sizeRisk.evidence: Well-scoped for 6 months. Risks identified with mitigations. Estimated: L (large) but manageable.

whyThisIsReferenceQuality: Goal is SMART: Specific outcome, measurable target (30%), time-bound deadline (Q2/2026).
Benefits are quantified for multiple stakeholders (customers, support, business) with concrete numbers.
Child stories are explicitly linked with status tracking (Done/In Progress/Backlog).
Success metrics include baseline, target, and deadline – enables objective success measurement.
Stakeholders are named with roles – clear accountability (Owner, Tech Lead, Support, Legal, UX).
Timeline has milestones with story mapping – enables progress tracking.
Risks are identified with mitigations – proactive risk management.
Dependencies on other teams are documented – enables cross-team coordination.
howToUseThisReference: Use as a template for structuring epics: Goal → Benefit → Stories → Metrics → Stakeholders → Timeline.
Compare your epic against this reference: Is your goal SMART (with numbers and deadline)?
Check if your benefits are as quantified as this reference (%, time, tickets, cost).
Ensure you have at least 2-3 child stories linked (this reference has 4).
Define success metrics with baseline and target – not just 'improve X'.
Name stakeholders explicitly – who owns this, who is impacted?
Use the quality criteria checklist to self-assess before refinement.
differencesFromStory: No 'As a user...' format – epics use outcome-oriented goal statement.
Focus on strategic outcome (30% reduction) vs. user feature (download PDF).
Spans multiple sprints (6 months) vs. single sprint (1-2 weeks).
Requires success metrics with baseline/target vs. acceptance criteria.
Requires stakeholder mapping vs. single user role.
Requires milestone timeline vs. sprint deadline.
